author: Dara Kerr and agencies
description:
Indira Talwani’s ruling presents major setback for president as first states begin to send out mail ballots for midterms

A federal judge on Friday again blocked Donald Trump’s executive order to impose sweeping restrictions on mail-in voting, the latest in a legal back-and-forth playing out less than two months before election day.

US district court judge Indira Talwani initially placed a temporary order blocking the president’s mandate and has now extended that prohibition with a stronger preliminary injunction. The ruling comes hours after North Carolina became the first state to start sending out mail-in ballots for the 3 November midterm elections.

Continue reading...
title: US judge extends block on Trump order to restrict mail-in voting

author: Marina Dunbar
description:
Jeffrey Mosteller pleaded no contest to charges relating to burning death of Thomas Cooper in Michigan

A former safety manager has been sentenced to one year and seven months in prison in connection with the death of a five-year-old Michigan boy who was killed in a fiery January 2025 explosion inside a hyperbaric oxygen chamber.

Jeffrey Mosteller, 66, received that sentence after pleading no contest to involuntary manslaughter in Oakland county circuit court in Michigan on Monday.

Continue reading...
title: Ex-safety manager given 19 months’ prison over five-year-old’s hyperbaric chamber fire death

author: Marina Dunbar
description:
Officials decline to confirm whether death was one of two announced last week as Lancaster county outbreak grows

A six-week-old child in Pennsylvania died from measles, the Lancaster County coroner has determined, following two measles-related deaths in the county last week.

The determination comes as Lancaster county faces a growing measles outbreak.

Continue reading...
title: Six-week-old child in Pennsylvania dies from measles, coroner says

author: Joseph Gedeon in Washington
description:
The president was moved to a separate aircraft during a July trip after officials learned of a possible Iranian threat, leaving questions about the plane’s defenses unanswered

Donald Trump intends to use the Boeing jet gifted by Qatar for his trip to Ireland next week, marking the first time the aircraft will leave the US since concerns were raised over whether it can adequately protect the president from attack.

The decision, a senior administration official told the Washington Post, comes weeks after Trump suggested the plane would be grounded for about a month while it underwent unspecified security upgrades.

Continue reading...
title: Trump to take gifted Qatar jet to Ireland despite questions about its security

author: Anna Isaac and Rowena Mason
description:
James Orr, an associate professor, was shown in Channel 4 News footage apparently trying to sidestep electoral law

Cambridge University has said it is examining the conduct of James Orr, its associate professor and a top Reform UK aide, after he was filmed appearing to try to circumvent electoral laws on foreign political donations.

Orr, the suspended head of policy for the party, is one of two senior officials to step aside after claims that he orchestrated a plot to have polling paid for by a foreign firm – something that is impermissible under British electoral law.

Continue reading...
title: Cambridge University probing conduct of academic suspended by Reform UK

author: Richard Adams Education editor
description:
Nazir Afzal to focus in review’s first stage on support given to professor in immediate period before his death

The University of Cambridge has asked Nazir Afzal, a former chief crown prosecutor for north-west England, to lead the first part of its review into the death of the scholar Jason Arday.

Arday died at his home in south London on 14 August, nine days after his resignation as a Cambridge professor amid swirling allegations of plagiarism and inconsistencies in statements about his career.

Continue reading...
title: Cambridge University asks former chief crown prosecutor to open Arday review

author: Michael Sainato
description:
Labor department report alleges Lori Chavez-DeRemer also made a staffer attend a strip club while on a personal trip

Donald Trump’s former secretary of labor, Lori Chavez-DeRemer, drank during working hours, kept alcohol on federal property and made a staffer attend a strip club while on a personal trip, according to a new report by the Department of Labor’s Office of Inspector General .

Chavez-DeRemer was appointed by Trump to serve as labor secretary in January 2025 and resigned in April 2026 amid the misconduct allegations.

Continue reading...
title: Trump’s ex-labor secretary drank on job and created ‘toxic’ work environment, report alleges

author: Geraldine McKelvie
description:
British Polling Council and Market Research Society announce inquiries into JL Partners, which has been accused of breaking transparency rules

  • What is the latest finance scandal facing Reform UK?

A polling firm at the centre of allegations that Reform UK breached electoral law is being investigated by two industry bodies.

JL Partners, which is run by former Conservative aides, has been accused of breaking transparency rules by failing to declare that three separate polls had been commissioned by the party.

Continue reading...
title: Investigations launched into polling firm at centre of Reform UK allegations

author: Edward Helmore
description:
Defense lawyer has asked for an hour to request emergency stay after jury deadlocked for third time

  • Lindsay Clancy murder trial: live updates

The judge in the trial of Lindsay Clancy, the Massachusetts mother accused of killing her three young children, plans to declare a mistrial after the jury could not reach a unanimous verdict and remained deadlocked after a week of deliberations.

Jurors in Plymouth state court spent more than 38 hours in deliberations over the charges against the 36-year-old mom, which came on the heels of a weeks-long trial that directed national attention to maternal mental health issues that can occur postpartum.
title: Judge set to declare mistrial in Lindsay Clancy case after jury deadlocked again

author: Ben Quinn Political correspondent
description:
Outlet faced significant financial challenges after it had funds blocked by bank without explanation

Workers at the leftwing news outlet the Canary fear it will not survive beyond this year amid access to funds being blocked and allegations of financial mismanagement and internal turmoil.

The site, which was founded in 2015 against a backdrop of the wave of support for the then Labour leader, Jeremy Corbyn, appeared set to expand after a multimillion-pound injection of funds last year.

Continue reading...
title: Canary staff not paid amid fears for news website’s future

author: Kate Connolly in Berlin, Lorenzo Tondo and Pjotr Sauer
description:
Belarusian said to have had tourist visa issued by Italy is investigated over alleged attempt to attack Leipzig airport

  • Europe live – latest updates

Germany is urging its European partners to introduce tighter limitations on Russian citizens entering the EU on tourist visas, after recent sabotage attacks which Berlin has blamed on Moscow.

German authorities are investigating a Belarusian national, who also holds a Russian passport, over the alleged attempt to attack Leipzig airport using drones and explosives.

Continue reading...
title: Germany urges EU to cut Russians’ holiday visas after sabotage attacks

author: Associated Press
description:
Jury starts seven day of deliberations after foreperson told judge juror won’t follow instruction about reasonable doubt

The deadlocked jury in the Lindsay Clancy trial started a seventh day of deliberations on Friday, a day after the jury’s foreperson told the judge a single juror would not follow the court’s instructions about reasonable doubt.

The extraordinary disclosure made in the form of a note delivered to the judge offered the clearest glimpse yet of what may be keeping jurors from reaching a verdict on whether the Massachusetts mother is criminally responsible for killing her three children.

Continue reading...
title: Deadlocked jury in Lindsay Clancy trial resumes deliberations after dispute

author: Peter Walker Senior political correspndent
description:
With senior party figures appearing split and leader’s favourability rating dropping, questions about donations are causing yet more headaches

  • UK politics live – latest updates

Midway through an event at Reform’s annual conference on Friday there was question for the audience: who was worried about a Channel 4 News exposé of potential wrongdoing by party officials over donations? Almost no hands went up. The faithful might be sanguine. But make no mistake, Nigel Farage faces yet another problem.

Careful plans have been again upset. After months of answering – or primarily dodging – questions about his own finance
title: Reform UK exposé comes just as Farage was hoping to change the narrative

author: Nick Evershed and Jonathan Barrett
description:
Cotality says prices have declined in most capital cities over winter. Search the data to see how they have changed in your area

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Australia’s property market is facing a rare price correction, as rising interest rates and less favourable tax settings for investors accelerate a downturn.

Most capital cities recorded winter price falls, according to Cotality data, with Sydney leading the decline. That weakness is expected to continue, as higher inflation could lead to
title: Australia’s housing prices are trending down. See which suburbs have had the biggest falls

author: Joanna Partridge
description:
Russian and Ukrainian strikes in July killed more crew than in whole war to that month, preventing grain exports

A summer of hostilities in the Black Sea proved deadly for seafarers, as Russia and Ukraine attacked each other’s ships and port infrastructure, preventing vital grain exports and prompting concerns that the conflict will push global food prices even higher.

More crew were killed in the Black Sea in July than during the entirety of the war before that month as the conflict has intensified, making the body of water the most dangerous in the world for commercial shipping. This is despite the conflict between the US and Iran, with vessels still being targeted in the strait of Hormuz, Red Sea and Gulf of Aden.
title: Deadly escalation in Black Sea attacks prompts fears of even higher food prices

author: Angela Giuffrida in Rome
description:
Lorena Isceri was thrown off a motorway bridge, allegedly by ex-boyfriend Federico Vella

A 45-year-old woman abducted and thrown off a motorway bridge near Florence has become the seventh alleged femicide in Italy since mid-August.

Lorena Isceri was abducted on Thursday afternoon, allegedly by her ex-boyfriend, Federico Vella, in the Rifredi area of Florence, before being forced into the boot of his car and driven towards a bridge on the A1 motorway.

In the UK, Samaritans can be contacted on freephone 116 123 and the domestic abuse helpline is 0808 2000 247. In the US, the suicide prevention lifeline is 988 and the domestic violence hotline is 1-800-799-SAFE (7233). In Australia, the crisis support service Lifeline is on 13 11 14 and the national
title: Woman, 45, killed in Florence in seventh alleged femicide in Italy since mid-August

author: Tom Phillips in Rio de Janeiro
description:
Abelardo De La Espriella posts video of himself with rows of body bags as performative populism continues to sweep Americas

Colombia’s hardline president, Abelardo De La Espriella, has provoked outrage after posting a video on social media in which he strides through rows of white body bags that he says contained the corpses of 23 “neutralised” guerrillas.

De La Espriella took power last month vowing “all-out war” against illegal armed groups and he published the footage on Thursday in an apparent attempt to show he was fulfilling that pledge.

Continue reading...
title: Colombia president provokes disgust by posing with bodies of guerrillas

author: Heather Stewart
description:
Bank of England governor says central bankers must explain decisions or risk being seen as ‘unrepresentative elite’

The governor of the Bank of England has said the rise of populist politicians presents a serious challenge to independent central banks.

As Nigel Farage’s Reform UK gathered for its annual conference in Birmingham, Andrew Bailey said central bankers must be prepared to explain their decisions to the public or risk being attacked as an “unrepresentative elite”.

Continue reading...
title: Populism poses serious challenge to independent central banks, Bailey says

author: Mark Brown North of England correspondent
description:
Five jailed after targeting victim and subjecting him to ordeal linked to past relationship breakdown

Dramatic footage shows a kidnapped man jumping from a first floor window into a tree before running into the street and, by chance, coming across a police car.

Lincolnshire police said the ordeal of the unnamed man had been “horrifying” and the presence of a marked police vehicle “may have saved his life”.

Continue reading...
title: Man jumps out of first floor window to escape kidnappers in Lincoln

author: Tamara Davison
description:
Family-run Al-Qarara Seed Bank is striving to help Palestinians gain sovereignty over their food security

Salama Ayesh Muhanna still remembers the first seeds he planted on his family’s land in al-Qarara, Gaza. At just 17, Muhanna had proudly sprouted cucumbers.

“I was very happy because I saw the results,” Muhanna says. “We were farmers at heart.”

Continue reading...
title: Seeds of hope: how a local farming project is offering a lifeline to Gaza

author: Reuters
description:
Senator releases letters from armed forces after reports of location data being used to track US troops in Middle East

US military officials say they have disabled advertising trackers on a range of phones and computers, according to letters released on Friday by the US senator Ron Wyden and ⁠statements given to Reuters.

The development follows reports ​that commercially available location data had been used to target American forces in the Middle East.

Continue reading...
title: US military disables ad trackers on troops’ phones amid security fears

author: Jamie Grierson and Steven Morris
description:
Nick Park began modelling the character as a feline, before finding it too difficult and changing him to a dog

The creator of Wallace and Gromit has revealed that the world’s most famous stop-motion animated dog was nearly a cat.

As Aardman Animations marks its 50th anniversary, Nick Park, who joined the studio in 1985, told the BBC he originally modelled Gromit as a feline companion for Wallace.

Continue reading...
title: Wallace’s dog Gromit was nearly a cat, reveals creator as Aardman turns 50

author: Sam Levin in Los Angeles
description:
In the California City facility, ‘contact visits’ are strictly forbidden – but detained residents aren’t staying quiet. Are officials listening?

Teresa Reyes drove 300 miles to be with her son on his 32nd birthday in May, but she couldn’t give him a gift, share a meal with him or give him a hug. She couldn’t even touch him.

Her son, Guillermo, a tattoo artist from San Jose, is locked up in the California City immigration detention center, California’s largest Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) facility, and the only way he can see his mother is behind a thick pane of glass.

Continue reading...
title: ICE bans hugging inside California’s largest detention center. Families are fighting back

author: Martin Belam
description:
Vice-president’s claim US-Iran conflict is not war draws ridicule from Democrat Ro Khanna. Plus, iconic feminist Gloria Steinem dies aged 92

  • Don’t already get First Thing in your inbox? Sign up here

Good morning. The US vice-president, JD Vance, has responded to claims that an American strike was responsible for killing four people, including a child, at a wedding celebration in southern Iran by saying that “sometimes things happen”. The deaths were reported by the Iranian Red Crescent, which operates independently of Tehran and is treated by most international monitors as a credible source on casualty figures.

In a further comment, described by the congressman Ro Khanna, a Democrat from California, as “gaslighting”, the vice-pres
title: JD Vance accused of ‘gaslighting’ after saying he is ‘skeptical’ US struck Iranian wedding  | First Thing

author: Tom Ambrose
description:
The decision marks a setback for Republicans in a national redistricting battle

  • Sign up for US Breaking News emails

Hello and welcome to the US politics live blog.

The Missouri supreme court blocked a Republican-drawn new congressional map ⁠from being used in November’s midterm ⁠elections, a blow to the party’s ​odds for maintaining its narrow US House majority.

The Trump administration filed an emergency request asking the US supreme court to lift order blocking USPS from implementing mail-in voting restrictions. Chuck Schumer said the president was “[attempting] to destroy the integrity of our elections” with the move.

Excava
title: Missouri supreme court blocks congressional maps backed by Trump for midterms – US politics live

author: Deepa Parent
description:
Mourning turns to anger as residents of Kuhestak say Baloch communities are being placed in path of conflict

People in Kuhestak, a predominantly Baloch city in Iran’s southern Hormozgan province, are mourning after a strike on a wedding killed at least four people, including a child, and injured more than 60, according to local authorities.

The blast hit at around 9.30pm on 1 September, turning a night of celebration into one of devastation for the small coastal community, which is on the strait of Hormuz.

Continue reading...
title: Iranian town mourns after deadly strike on wedding

author: Daniella Lucas
description:
As one card recently sold for £12m, opportunistic thefts have surged – envelopes are being opened en route, costing small businesses thousands

Pokémon’s success over the last 30 years has seen it grow from a much-loved Game Boy classic, to a world-dominating brand with TV shows, spin-off games, toys and even a theme park. The trading card game is a huge part of that, with more than 85bn cards printed over its lifetime, and the appetite for them shows no signs of slowing down. Packs get snapped up after release so quickly it’s now almost impossible to find them in shops, and a booming resale market is driving the hobby into murky waters.

One card recently sold for an eye-watering £12m, and an inc
title: Thieves target mail order sales as Pokémon card prices soar

author: Mark Sweney
description:
Firm has celebrity fans and ambassadors including Prince Harry, Jennifer Aniston and Kim Kardashian

Fans of Oura are accustomed to using its trendy smart rings to fastidiously monitor their health but now investors are preparing to track a new metric – its share price.

The San Francisco-headquartered company’s filing to imminently list on the Nasdaq stock exchange in New York was made public on Thursday.

Continue reading...
title: Health-tracking smart ring maker Oura to list on US stock market

author: Kiran Stacey Policy editor
description:
Ed Miliband says Britain’s position remains ‘unwavering’ in response to remarks by Argentina’s president

  • UK politics live – latest updates

British ministers have hit back after the Argentinian president said “winds of change” favourable to his country’s claim to the Falklands were “blowing around the world”.

The foreign secretary, Ed Miliband, said the UK would “resolutely uphold” the self-determination of the islands after the Argentinian president, Javier Milei, said his country needed to take them back.
title: UK ministers hit back at Argentinian Falklands claim and insist islands remain British

author: Joanna Partridge and Alex Daniel
description:
Intensification of Middle East conflict and ongoing Russian export ban sees diesel prices rise 10% in less than a week

Farmers are facing an “astronomical” jump in the price of fuel needed to operate their vehicles and machinery after a surge in diesel costs in the UK and US.

Renewed fighting between the US and Iran has driven up the price of crude oil, while last week Russia extended a ban on diesel exports, further pushing up market prices.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Astronomical’ fuel price surge hits farmers in UK and US

author: Andrew Sparrow
description:
James Orr and Dan Jukes, aides to Nigel Farage, stepped down after an investigation by Channel 4

Nigel Farage has been speaking about the undercover donations investigaton. He says the party has “broken no laws” and has not “taken any dodgy money”.

In a separate interview, on Times Radio, Lee Anderson, the Reform UK chief whip and party chair, insisted there was no chance of Nigel Farage resigning over the undercover investigation into party donations.

I don’t think Nigel has got any questions on this. The two people involved, they have gone. They have left the building. I keep saying this time and time again. They have gone. That is the right thing to do. They are not coming back and Nigel is going nowhere …

Nigel is an honest man. I have known him for many years now. The party has done the right thing by launching this investigation. Nigel will be on the main stage later on explaining our first 100 days in government. He i
title: Reform officials suspended over donations investigation will not ‘come back’, says party chair – UK politics live

author: Jakub Krupa
description:
The efforts are part of an ongoing attempt to cripple the country’s power grid ahead of winter

Russia keeps targeting Ukraine’s energy facilities in its latest round of overnight attacks, part of an ongoing attempt to cripple the country’s power grid ahead of winter.

Odesa region governor Oleh Kiper said that one was died and at least five were injured in the attack.

Continue reading...
title: Russia maintains attacks on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure – Europe live

author: Kiran Stacey Policy editor
description:
Energy secretary could recommend new North Sea drilling next week, as ministers also consider approval for Rosebank oilfield

  • UK politics live – latest updates

  • Business live – latest updates

Ministers are poised to approve a controversial new gasfield in the North Sea this month, according to government sources, and are considering approving a major oilfield later this year.

Miatta Fahnbulleh, the energy secretary, will give her recommendation to approve the Jackdaw field off the coast of Aberdeen as soon as next week, according to people close to the decision, and the formal approval could follow
title: Jackdaw gasfield set to be approved by ministers this month, sources say

author: Raphael Rashid in Seoul
description:
Seoul reportedly seeking parliamentary approval to send military assets to Middle East but president’s office plays down claims

South Korea is reviewing a possible deployment of military assets to the strait of Hormuz amid pressure from Donald Trump over Seoul’s reluctance to provide support in the region, according to domestic media reports.

Citing unnamed government and military sources, the reportspublished on Thursday and Friday said preparations were under way and that the government intended to seek parliamentary approval for a new deployment. The reports, which appeared in major South Korean outlets, said the exact scale and timing have not been agreed.

Continue reading...
title: South Korea pushes back on reports it is readying Hormuz deployment amid US pressure

author: Press Association
description:
James Orr and Dan Jukes have stepped down from positions pending outcome of party investigation, says Reform UK

Two key aides to Nigel Farage have stepped down from their roles pending the outcome of an investigation by Reform UK into a broadcast by Channel 4 News alleging they breached political donation rules, a party spokesperson said.

James Orr and Dan Jukes are alleged to have breached donation rules by having polling paid for by an overseas company.

Continue reading...
title: Farage aides step down after undercover report on Reform UK donations

author: Jamie Grierson
description:
Collective training exercises for UK-based units to be suspended for most of this year amid budget pressures

The British army has been ordered to halt non-essential training exercises in an effort to save money.

Troops preparing to be deployed or on deployments, those who are on standby or in a quick-reaction role will continue to train as normal. But collective training exercises for UK-based units are being suspended for most of this year amid budget pressures.

Continue reading...
title: British army told to halt non-essential training exercises to save money

author: Penry Buckley
description:
Charles says claims by developer Jean Nassif in an intercepted phone call that ‘we’re reshuffling the government’ did not reflect promises allegedly made to Nassif

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The younger brother of Dominic Perrottet has denied asking his brother to appoint a cabinet minister to achieve outcomes for a property developer, a corruption inquiry has heard.

Charles Perrottet told the Independent Commission Against Corruption (Icac) on Friday that claims made in an intercep
title: Charles Perrottet denies asking brother as premier to appoint cabinet minister, Icac hears

author: Graham Readfearn Environment and climate correspondent
description:
‘Challenging’ weather conditions and lack of snowfall are being blamed after a winter that broke multiple heat records

  • Sign up for climate and environment editor Adam Morton’s free Clear Air newsletter here

Major Australian alpine resorts are closing their ski operations up to a month early after a winter that broke multiple records for heat with limited snow falls being washed away by rain.

Predictions in June that a building El Niño could combine with global heating for a challenging ski season came to pass, with seven resorts either already closed or announcing ski lifts will stop operating this weekend.
title: Australian ski resorts to close up to a month early due to global heating and El Niño

author: Joanna Partridge
description:
National Audit Office urges government to act as climate crisis, disease and cyberattacks pose growing risks

The climate crisis, disease and cyber-attacks pose growing risks to the UK’s food supplies and the government needs to act to make the system more resilient, according to the public spending watchdog.

The National Audit Office (NAO) is urging the Department for Food, the Environment and Rural Affairs (Defra) to work more closely with households, communities and businesses to ensure the flow of crucial food into the country can withstand supply shocks that are becoming increasingly common and severe.

Continue reading...
title: UK has not done enough to prepare for shocks to food supplies, says watchdog

author: Rachel Salvidge
description:
Exclusive: As millions of people face hosepipe bans, many companies are not required to report, let alone cut, use of public supply

Less than 1% of businesses in England use more water than the daily needs of 10 million people, as millions of households face hosepipe bans and three-quarters of the country is in drought.

Businesses across England use 2.6bn litres a day from the public water supply, which includes potable and non-potable water provided by water companies. In total, businesses account for about 30% of public supply use, with two-thirds of their consumption in water-stressed areas, according to Mosl, the organisation that operates England’s business water market.

Continue reading...
title: Revealed: how companies ‘secretly’ use billions of litres of public water in drought-hit England

author: Tiago Rogero South America correspondent
description:
President cites Donald Trump’s suggestion that he might reconsider US support for British sovereignty, and threatens swifter sanctions on British oil interests

President Javier Milei has said “winds of change favourable” to Argentina’s claim to the Falkland Islands were “blowing around the world” in a televised address, citing signs that Donald Trump might reconsider the US position on the islands’ sovereignty.

“Recently, President Trump declared that the US is re-evaluating its historic position in relation to the Malvinas,” he said, using the Argentinian name for the islands.

Continue reading...
title: President Javier Milei says ‘winds of change’ support Argentina’s claim to Falkland Islands

author: Ashifa Kassam in Magdeburg
description:
As polls point to victory in Saxony-Anhalt for AfD party promising deportations, people face agonising choice: stay or go

As the Bible study session wrapped up, leaving worshippers to mingle over cake and coffee, Fatemeh, 44, fought back tears as the conversation turned to Sunday’s state election in Saxony-Anhalt.

“I worry about it every day,” she said. “I can’t stop thinking about my son and what might happen to us.”

Fatemeh worries about what might happen after the elections. Photograph: Christian Jungeblodt/The Guardian

Continue reading...
title: ‘This could just be the beginning’: minorities fear first far-right win in German state election

author: Adam Morton
description:
New record for Australia as more than 27,000 EVs sold in August, driven by the rising cost of fuel and new government policy

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Electric vehicle sales in Australia exceeded petrol cars for the first time last month as a transformation driven by high fuel prices and government policy encouraging clean car uptake accelerated.

More than 27,000 EVs were sold in August, a new record for a single month and representing 24.9% of new cars sold. The climate-friendly t
title: EV sales outpace petrol cars for first time as Australians dodge soaring fuel costs

author: Australian Associated Press
description:
Daniel Billings said ‘I did what I did’ in call from friend’s house after 2024 domestic violence murder

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Two hours after Daniel Billings murdered his ex-girlfriend Molly Ticehurst in a frenzied stabbing, he spoke to a woman he had met on Tinder.

“I’m sorry I murdered her,” Billings told the woman during a phone call at 2.02am on 22 April 2024.
title: Molly Ticehurst’s killer called woman he’d met on Tinder after stabbing and said ‘I’m sorry I murdered her’, court hears

author: Eromo Egbejule in Abidjan
description:
Togo-sponsored resolution calls to phase out traditional map that depicts continent as similar size to Greenland

The UN general assembly will vote on Friday on a resolution for the world to formally phase out the traditional Mercator map of the globe in favour of one that more accurately displays Africa’s size.

Robert Dussey, Togo’s foreign affairs minister, said the resolution was sponsored by Togo and backed by countries including the African Union’s 54 other member states. He did not specify the total number.

Continue reading...
title: UN to vote on adopting new world map that shows Africa’s true scale

author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
description:
Republican candidate Thomas Ross and former campaign manager allegedly devised plan to stash drugs in rival Louise Secker’s purse or vehicle

A Missouri House race has been rocked by the Wednesday arrest of Republican candidate Thomas Ross, whom prosecutors accuse of attempting to frame his primary opponent Louise Secker for cocaine possession.

In June, Ross allegedly gave his former campaign manager, identified by the initials “CS” in court documents, a bag of cocaine and Adderall. The two allegedly devised a plan for the former manager to stash the drugs in Secker’s purse or vehicle.

Continue re
title: Missouri state legislative candidate accused of trying to plant cocaine on opponent

author: Associated Press
description:
Telle has previously worked for Trump during his first term as a special assistant to the president for legislative affairs

Donald Trump on Thursday named Adam Telle as the acting army secretary after the departure of Daniel Driscoll amid widespread reports of tensions with defense secretary Pete Hegseth.

Telle is currently the assistant secretary of the army for civil works.

Continue reading...
title: Trump names Adam Telle as acting army secretary following the departure of Driscoll

author: Danny Monteverde  of WWL Louisiana
description:
Sean Alfortish and Leon Parker convicted on some counts but not murder charges linked to insurance fraud plot

A federal jury in New Orleans on Thursday returned a split verdict after more than 30 hours of deliberations in a three-week-long blockbuster fraud and murder trial that garnered headlines far beyond Louisiana.

Jurors deadlocked on murder charges Sean Alfortish and Leon “Chunky” Parker faced, leading US district judge Wendy Vitter to declare a mistrial as prosecutors vowed to try the case on those counts again.

Continue reading...
title: Split verdict in New Orleans murder trial tied to staged-wrecks scheme
